search_log: Searched “Iron Flame Rebecca Yarros official excerpt chapter first person Violet,” “point of view first person narrator Xaden final chapter,” the author's site, Hachette, and Google Books.
Opened the author and Hachette title pages; both verified the work and Violet-centered premise, but their accessible text was synopsis rather than diagnostic narrative prose.

Located TODAY's authorized prepublication excerpt, but the original page was blocked by robots.txt; syndicated/search copies showed first-person prose, so it was treated as a discovery lead rather than cited as Tier A evidence.

Searched targeted combinations for “first-person POV,” “Violet's point of view,” “final chapter Xaden,” and narrative perspective; opened and compared whole-book structural descriptions and the Princeton discussion guide.

Follow-up research found no credible claim that any sustained section is narrated in second or third person; sources consistently describe Violet's perspective with a final Xaden point-of-view chapter.
person_note: The diagnostic Goodreads passages repeatedly expose Violet as a participating first-person narrator in event narration and in narration surrounding dialogue. Web research corroborates that Violet controls nearly the entire novel and that Chapter 66 switches to Xaden's viewpoint. That switch does not warrant ALTERNATING because both narrators narrate as “I”; multiple first-person narrators remain FIRST under the methodology. Dialogue, aphorisms, and epigraph-like correspondence were kept separate from base narration. Confidence is medium because the accessible web support consists chiefly of explicit reviews and structural guides; the authorized TODAY excerpt could not be opened directly.
